title: Chào bạn
summary: A friendly neutral greeting for peers and warm casual help.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Chào bạn is the friendly version of hello when bạn fits the relationship. It works with peers, friendly helpers, classmates, younger adults near your age, or someone whose role feels casual rather than formal. If the person is clearly older or in a service role, Chào anh or Chào chị may sound warmer.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Use Chào bạn when you want a warm but simple hello and do not need to show extra age-based respect.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: The greeting is short, but bạn changes the relationship it creates.

sections.title: Natural variations
sections.body: Switch the last word when the relationship is clearer.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use it with a friendly guide, a peer at a class or tour, a casual local helper, or someone who has already made the exchange feel relaxed. In a formal service moment, start with Xin chào or Dạ, chào anh/chị.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Bạn is useful, but it is not a perfect universal you. Vietnamese often prefers relationship words, so Chào bạn is best when you truly want a friendly neutral tone.

sections.title: Explore next
sections.body: After a friendly hello, these are natural next moves.
